east_texas.headline: Patchy fog early, then mild and mostly sunny.
east_texas.summary: Patchy fog in low spots until about 9 AM, then a mostly sunny, mild afternoon in the low 70s. Warm and dry weather holds through Saturday. A cold front Sunday brings little rain and cooler air for Thanksgiving week.

days.text: Sunny and mild. Patchy fog possible early.
Partly sunny. A slight chance of showers Saturday night.
Cold front. Most areas get less than a tenth of an inch, some none.
Near to a bit below normal. Lows in the upper 30s to low 40s.

facts.p: About 40 customers out in Smith County
Lows stay above freezing through Wed

panels.title: Cooler, but not Arctic
paras: After Sunday's front, NWS Shreveport expects temperatures near late-November normals, perhaps slightly below by Tuesday. The Climate Prediction Center leans below normal for the Southern Plains Nov 24 – Dec 2.

Rain looks limited through the holiday. Better rain chances may come just after Thanksgiving, but details are uncertain. Some single model runs show a big storm that weekend; most guidance does not support that yet.

panels.title: A strong El Niño is in charge
paras: El Niño is now strong and still strengthening, near +2.5°C in the key Pacific region. That usually means an active southern storm track, with more rain and more cool, cloudy days in East Texas.
It does not bring Arctic air on its own. Ice or snow still needs cold air from Canada, and Canada is running warm right now.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, KLTV closings, PowerOutage.us.

nm.headline: Quiet today, windy Friday, then a cold front with light snow Saturday.
nm.summary: Sunny and dry today after a very cold morning in the high valleys. West wind gusts near 35 mph Friday in the high country. A quick system Friday night into Saturday brings a dusting to a couple of inches in the northern mountains, followed by the coldest night of the season so far.

days.text: Sunny and windy. West wind 15–20 mph in the high country.
Scattered snow showers in the northern mountains. Snow levels drop sharply behind the front.
Coldest night of the season so far. Colder in sheltered valleys.
Another quick system with low mountain snow chances.

nm.snow_note: Tuesday night's snow added a little at the higher stations. Lower and sunny slopes are mostly bare.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu reports 6 in. of snow in the past week and a 5 in. base, which includes man-made snow. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Coldest night of the season Saturday
paras: NWS Albuquerque says Saturday's front may be the strongest of the season so far for temperature change, dropping temps 10 to 20 degrees. Expect teens and 20s across the northern mountains Saturday night, with colder readings in high valleys like the Moreno Valley. Angel Fire already reached about 12° this morning. Protect outdoor pipes and pets.

panels.title: Wet spots on two mountain routes
paras: NMRoads lists US-64 through Taos Canyon and NM-38 between Questa and Red River as difficult, with wet roads that may be slick. No closures on NM-518, NM-434, NM-75 or the interstates as of this morning.
No critical fire weather is expected.

panels.title: Strong El Niño favors a snowier season
paras: El Niño is strong and still strengthening. It usually sends more storms across the southern Rockies, which improves the odds for snowfall in the northern New Mexico mountains. It doesn't guarantee a big season, but the odds lean our way.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, Sipapu snow report, OnTheSnow projected openings, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
